title: Long CMCSA — NBCUniversal + Sky Tax-Free Spinoff Unlocks Sum-of-Parts Re-Rating
entry: Buy CMCSA at Monday June 29 open in the $28.00–$30.00 zone. Pre-market is +23-25% to $28.67 on the spinoff announcement, but tax-free de-conglomeration re-ratings historically sustain 15-25% premium for weeks as the market builds sum-of-parts models. Do not chase above $31 on Day 1 — buy the opening print or limit orders at $28.50–$29.50. The initial reaction is broad and retail-driven; institutional sum-of-parts model builds that add more sophisticated price target upgrades take 2-5 sessions. Size 4% of gross.
stop_loss: $25.00 daily close (~12.8% below $28.67 open) — implies either (1) a material regulatory obstacle emerges (FCC, DOJ) that casts doubt on the tax-free structure, (2) NBCUniversal SpinCo is valued by analysts at near-zero (the media assets are viewed as liabilities, not assets — a legitimate risk given Paramount's troubled valuation history), or (3) the broader equity market (SPX) falls more than 8% from current levels, dragging CMCSA down with it regardless of the idiosyncratic catalyst. A $25 close would put CMCSA near its pre-announcement price, implying the spinoff premium has been fully erased.
targets: $32.00 — first post-announcement wave: sell-side analysts build pure-play broadband CMCSA models; Comcast retains broadband, wireless, and cable with 32M subscribers; at Charter-comparable 7.5x EBITDA multiple on ~$20B broadband EBITDA, broadband stub alone worth $28-30/share; incremental SpinCo value credit begins; +11.6% from $28.67 open

$36.00 — NBCUniversal SpinCo begins receiving institutional valuation modeling; Peacock streaming + theme parks + broadcast networks + Universal Studios + Sky valued as comparable to Warner Bros. Discovery at improved optionality (no legacy-debt anchor); sell-side consensus PT upgrades reach $36-38; sum-of-parts valuation fully articulated; +25.6%

$40.00 — SpinCo IPO date confirmed, regulatory approvals progressing; CMCSA (broadband-only) trades at pure-play cable/connectivity infrastructure multiples (Altice, Frontier comparables compressed by leverage; CMCSA broadband now the cleanest such asset globally); +39.5%
catalyst: Comcast announced June 29, 2026 (pre-market) that it will spin off NBCUniversal and Sky into a separate publicly traded company through a tax-free transaction, targeting completion within approximately 12 months. The remaining Comcast entity retains broadband, wireless, and cable services — effectively becoming a pure-play connectivity infrastructure company. NBCUniversal SpinCo will include: Peacock, Bravo and NBCU linear networks, NBC/Telemundo broadcast, Universal Pictures and TV Studios, theme parks (including Universal), and Sky (European pay-TV and broadband). CMCSA surged 23-25% pre-market to $28.67 from a prior close near $23.30. The deal unlocks the conglomerate discount: for years, Comcast's broadband multiple has been suppressed by the linear-media drag from NBCUniversal (declining advertising, streaming losses). A clean separation allows the broadband business — one of the most cash-generative infrastructure assets in the US — to trade at its intrinsic multiple.
thesis:
Comcast's NBCUniversal/Sky spinoff is the archetypal conglomerate-discount unlock event. Broadband-only Comcast is a different asset from conglomerate Comcast. The company generates approximately $20-21B in broadband EBITDA annually from its 32M broadband subscriber base — one of the highest-margin, most cash-generative infrastructure businesses in the US. For years, this asset has been burdened by the trading multiple of a media conglomerate, weighted down by Peacock streaming losses ($2-3B/year in recent years), NBC linear advertising declines, and the operational complexity of running simultaneously the largest US cable operator and a major Hollywood studio. The spinoff removes this structural drag.

Tax-free de-conglomeration transactions have a documented pattern of sustained re-rating. The transaction is structured as a tax-free spinoff to Comcast shareholders — meaning no immediate tax event, which maximizes the economic value transfer compared to an asset sale. Broadband-only CMCSA at a pure-play infrastructure multiple (7–8x EBITDA) on $20B EBITDA implies a $140-160B equity value; current total CMCSA market cap at $28.67 × ~4.1B shares = ~$117B. There is meaningful valuation gap even before attributing any value to NBCUniversal SpinCo. Charter Communications trades at ~6.5x EBITDA on a more-leveraged broadband asset; Comcast's better balance sheet and larger subscriber base deserve a premium.

NBCUniversal SpinCo is not worthless — the market will discover this over the next 6-12 weeks. Universal Studios theme parks alone generated ~$9B revenue pre-pandemic and have recovered significantly. Sky adds a European broadband and pay-TV platform with 21M subscribers. Peacock has 40M+ subscribers. NBC broadcast retains the most valuable linear sports rights in the US (NFL, Super Bowl, Olympics). While media assets face secular challenges, the spinoff structure allows SpinCo to manage its own capital allocation without being subordinated to broadband capex cycles. Comparable transactions (WarnerMedia/AT&T spinoff, Viacom/CBS merger-then-split) show that even challenged media assets receive initial public market valuation premiums that sustain 3-6 months post-spin.

The counter-party argues: (1) Comcast is spinning off NBCUniversal because it is a liability, not an asset — management is offloading the streaming losses and linear decline onto shareholders; (2) the broadband business faces competitive pressure from fixed wireless access (T-Mobile, Verizon) and new fiber competitors, limiting the multiple expansion to current levels; (3) the spinoff takes 12 months to complete — ample time for the market to fade the initial 23% pop as regulatory risk (FCC, potential DOJ review of Sky) adds uncertainty. These risks are why the position is sized at 4% and the stop is firm at $25.
bull_case: Board and FCC approvals confirmed by September 2026. Sell-side analysts (Morgan Stanley, Wells Fargo) initiate on post-spin CMCSA at $38-40 PT based on 7.5x pure-play broadband EBITDA. NBCUniversal SpinCo receives initial institutional valuation of $30-35B (comparable to Paramount at better asset quality). CMCSA to $36 (Target 2) within 6 weeks; SpinCo anticipated IPO drives further premium. Optional: if SpinCo IPO is oversubscribed and values the entity above sell-side models, CMCSA broadband stub re-rates to $40 (Target 3) as the sum-of-parts valuation becomes universally accepted.
bear_case: DOJ/FCC signals concern about Sky acquisition (European telecom regulator review required). Analyst consensus: NBCUniversal SpinCo is structurally loss-making and will trade at 4-5x EBITDA maximum (below SpinCo's projected $3-4B EBITDA). Broadband competitive pressure from T-Mobile fixed-wireless accelerates; Comcast subscriber growth guided below 1% for 2027. CMCSA fades from $28.67 back toward $25 (stop) as the de-conglomeration premium erodes on regulatory uncertainty.
invalidation: $25.00 daily close; OR FCC or DOJ signals a formal second request for information (implies 6-18 month regulatory delay beyond the 12-month target); OR SpinCo valuation models from 3+ sell-side analysts place NBCUniversal/Sky below $20B total value (implying negative SpinCo EV after assumed debt load); OR CMCSA Q2 2026 earnings (late July) reveal broadband subscriber net losses exceeding 200K in the quarter (competitive pressure thesis validates); OR broad SPX correction exceeds 10% before July quarter-end
